## 6. Internal history versus observable value

One of the strongest pieces of the TOL formalization was the explicit refusal to collapse different causal histories merely because their outputs coincide.

Let the history-bearing state space be:

\[
\widetilde{\mathcal C}=(\mathcal C,h).
\]

Then it is permitted that:

\[
\boxed{
\widetilde L\widetilde R(x)
\neq
\widetilde R\widetilde L(x)
}
\]

internally.

An observation/projection map:

\[
q:
\widetilde{\mathcal C}
\rightarrow
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{observable}}
\]

can nevertheless satisfy:

\[
\boxed{
q(\widetilde L\widetilde R(x))
=
q(\widetilde R\widetilde L(x))
=
q(\widetilde O(x))
}
\]

This was called **confluence modulo the observable quotient**.

Equivalently, define:

\[
x\sim_q y
\iff
q(x)=q(y).
\]

Then different histories can be observationally equivalent without becoming the same derivation.

Core rule:

\[
\boxed{
\text{equivalent observation}
\not\Rightarrow
\text{identical derivation}
}
\]

This became a provenance-preservation principle and later aligns directly with SUN V2's rule that equal relational effect does not imply equal path/address.

## 13. 3-limit multiplicative group

The most mature recovered algebraization defined:

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal H_3
=
\{2^a3^b:a,b\in\mathbb Z\}
}
\]

as a 3-limit multiplicative group.

Under the prime-exponent coordinate map:

\[
\boxed{
\nu_{2,3}(2^a3^b)=(a,b)
}
\]

multiplication becomes vector addition.

The primitive operators map to:

\[
R=\frac23
\mapsto
(1,-1)
\]

\[
L=\frac34
\mapsto
(-2,1)
\]

\[
O=\frac12
\mapsto
(-1,0).
\]

Therefore:

\[
\boxed{
\nu(R)+\nu(L)
=
(1,-1)+(-2,1)
=
(-1,0)
=
\nu(O)
}
\]

This gives an additive coordinate representation of the harmonic closure identity.

## 14. Unevaluated versus evaluated harmonic spaces

To preserve operation order/history, the harmonic IR was split:

\[
\widetilde{\mathcal H}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal H.
\]

An evaluation quotient:

\[
\boxed{
q_H=\operatorname{eval}:
\widetilde{\mathcal H}
\rightarrow
\mathcal H
}
\]

permits:

\[
RL\neq LR
\quad\text{in }\widetilde{\mathcal H}
\]

while:

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{eval}(RL)
=
\operatorname{eval}(LR)
=
\operatorname{eval}(O)
=
\frac12
}
\]

in the evaluated harmonic space.

This is the harmonic-specific version of history-aware projected confluence.

A domain realization:

# PART XX — WHAT WAS NOT FINISHED

## 26. Unfinished formal work

Despite substantial algebraization, the recovered archive does **not** establish a final locked standalone "TOL Algebra v1.0".

Outstanding work includes:

### A. Complete type system

The role vocabulary exists, but a complete formal type judgment system was not recovered, e.g.:

\[
\Gamma\vdash f:A\rightarrow B.
\]

### B. Full domain/codomain specification

Every primitive and composite operator still needs explicit legal domains, codomains, partiality rules, and failure semantics.

### C. Identity and associativity laws

The archive contains composition semantics but not a complete presentation proving all category/algebra axioms.

### D. Closure theorem

The system still needs a proof specifying exactly under what operator vocabulary it is closed.

### E. Complete address algebra

TOL became an address/topology system, but the address transformations themselves were not fully axiomatized.

### F. Unitization/class algebra

Later SUN V2 introduces class, unitization, register, and address transitions more cleanly than the original TOL work. These need to be integrated without allowing TOL to manufacture SUN's native invariant.

### G. Residual metric calibration

\(\varepsilon\) is defined structurally, and \(\|\varepsilon\|_w\) was proposed, but the weights and comparison metric were not locked.

### H. Faithfulness criteria

The preservation set is known conceptually, but exact mathematical conditions for faithful/partial/invalid realization remain to be formalized.

### I. Boundary semantics

Malkhut/boundary quotient is a strong candidate model, not a universally proved property of every Tree representation.

### J. Historical versus structural evidence ledger

The project explicitly distinguishes historical descent from independent structural recurrence, but this distinction still needs a formal evidence schema if TOL becomes executable.

### K. Standalone canonical specification

Most importantly: the work evolved through several documents. It was never recovered as one frozen canonical TOL specification with versioning, axioms, proofs, test vectors, and lock status.

derivation.domain: Finite ordered words in the recovered R,L,O scalar factors, with positive reference C. The statement concerns evaluation and separately retained histories, not a new physical sound-generation model.
derivation.effective_counts: N_R=r+o; N_L=l+o. If q(w)/C=2^a3^b, then N_R=-a-2b and N_L=-a-b.
derivation.proof: Substitute a=r-2l-o and b=l-r. Then -a-2b=r+o and -a-b=l+o. Unique prime factorization makes (a,b) unique for a positive rational in the 3-limit group. Therefore two words have equal scalar evaluation exactly when their effective count pairs coincide.
derivation.normal_form_boundary: R^N_R L^N_L represents the same scalar evaluation, not the same protected history. Replacing O by RL and commuting R/L is permissible only after evaluation.
derivation.consequence: Scalar output cannot recover RL versus LR, or any exact ordered path in a fiber with multiple protected histories. A bridge claiming to preserve history must carry independent path information or a richer observable.
derivation.no_scalar_history_left_inverse: If protected histories u=RL and v=LR are distinct but q(u)=q(v), no function s from scalar outputs back to histories can satisfy s∘q=id on a domain containing both: s(q(u))=s(q(v)) would force u=v. This follows from the recovered two-path example without assuming that every longer word is distinct.
derivation.path_information_example: With six R and six L operations, 924 ordered word records share ratio 1/64.
